own_original_text:
An application having been duly made, pursuant to and in full compliance with the provisions of title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, for my approval of a Code of Fair Competition for the Textile Machinery Manufacturing Industry, and hearings having been held thereon and the Administrator having rendered his report containing an analysis of the said code of fair competition together with his recommendations and findings with respect thereto, and the Administrator having found that the said code of fair competition complies in all respects with the pertinent provisions of title I of said act and that the requirements of clauses (1) and (2) of subsection (a) of section 3 of the said act have been met:

Now, Therefore, I, Franklin 1). Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority vested in me by title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do approve the report and recommendations and adopt the findings of the Administrator and do order that the said code of fair competition be and it is hereby approved.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

Approval recommended:

     Hugh S. Johnson.

          Administrator.

The White House,

October 3, 1933.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the census register lists EO 6310 dated 1933-10-03 (Franklin D. Roosevelt); the WPA 1944 list entry for 1933 Oct 3, p.541, records the code for the Textile Machinery Manufacturing Industry as approved, and the held text's date and subject agree. APP page check passed: the mirror page record with the held text's sha256 (common-crawl capture) has a heading naming this order's number, the same date and subject, and a text_sha256 equal to the held text's. The held text was read in full. Own terms: the order has no stated period, condition, "until" date, "pending" or provisional wording. Repeal route per the reviewed shared analysis: an approval under section 3 depended on the code approval and enforcement provisions that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed on June 14, 1935; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded only as a validity characterization.

savings_residuals.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued; the NIRA section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the code during the period is an accrued effect for past action only. The proviso in section 2 of the resolution limits the section 5 exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful, names agreements rather than codes and states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for past action. Nothing held continues the approval after June 14, 1935.

versions.research_rationale:
The held American Presidency Project transcription of EO:6310 is a one-command order: after reciting the application, hearings and the Administrator's findings under section 3(a) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, the President wrote "do order that the said code of fair competition be and it is hereby approved" for the Code of Fair Competition for the Textile Machinery Manufacturing Industry. It states no period, condition, "until" date, provisional approval or exception, so no own-terms end applies. The command depends wholly on section 3 of Title I. Under the reviewed shared analysis, the first end of such a command is the statutory repeal on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 section 2, "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; approved June 14, 1935) unless a held record shows an earlier cancellation or suspension, and none is held for this code.
